newsitem.title: USA: Cargill says not advised it target of gov't probe.
newsitem.headline: Cargill says not advised it target of gov't probe.

text.p: Cargill Inc said it has not been informed that it is a target in the widespread government investigation of major agricultural firms for possible price fixing in the feed additive industry.

In a statement from the company dated January 24 and received by Reuters on January 30, Cargill said it was asked by the Justice Department for information related to the company's citric acid and high fructose corn syrup businesses, and that it has "fully complied with those requests.
"However, at no time has Cargill been advised that it is a target of the government investigations," the statement said.

On Wednesday, a U.S. subsidiary of the German pharmaceutical and chemical giant Bayer AG pleaded guilty to fixing the price of a key food additive and agreed to pay a $50 million fine - the second highest criminal antitrust fine ever, second only to the $100 million fine charged to Archer-Daniels-Midland Co last year for price fixing in the lysine market.

The Justice Department said Wednesday that other firms are still being investigated in its probe of the citric acid industry, but would not reveal their identities. The government is also continuing its investigation of the big high fructose corn syrup market, but has so far not charged any company or individual in that part of the probe.

The Cargill statement maintained that the company is innocent of any wrongdoing, and "has conducted itself properly, competing openly and ethically." It said it is confident the government probe will confirm that.

The statement also referred to civil cases arising out of the federal investigation, and said that even though Cargill has been named as a defendent in some of the suits, they have no merit and "were prompted by publicity surrounding the federal investigation, not evidence of improper or illegal activity on our part."

In December, four companies agreed to pay a total of $94 million to settle a class-action lawsuit filed by food processors in California. Cargill was named as the fifth defendant but did not join the settlement.
